title: Applied ML Quality Guardrails and Regression Triage Playbook
author: Aisha Patel
content:
Overview:

This playbook consolidates Redwood’s applied-ML practices for building and maintaining quality guardrails, integrating the eval harness, defining prompt sets and benchmarks, onboarding models for serving, selecting quantization profiles, and triaging regressions. It is intended for ML engineers, SREs, and product owners responsible for model quality in production.

Scope:
- Covers automated and human-in-the-loop guardrails for generation and embeddings workloads
- Includes eval harness integration conventions, prompt set lifecycle, and regression detection thresholds
- Applies to hosted, dedicated, and private deployments of serving models

Goals:
- Detect and block substantive quality regressions before user impact
- Provide clear, repeatable triage steps that reduce mean-time-to-diagnosis (MTTD)
- Standardize quantization guidance to balance latency/cost and output fidelity

Roles & Ownership:
- Model Owner (ML Eng): maintains prompt sets, model evals, and onboard config
- Guardrails Lead (Applied ML): defines quality thresholds and continuous evals
- Deployment Owner (Infra/SRE): rollout/rollback automation and observability alerts
- Customer Success: validation for customer-facing regressions and incident comms

Guardrail Types (high-level):
1) Functional correctness: task-specific pass/fail (e.g., extraction accuracy, intent classification)
2) Hallucination and factuality: entity hallucination rates, unsupported assertions
3) Safety and policy: toxic content detection, PII exposures, disallowed outputs
4) Performance regressions: median/95th token latency, token generation throughput, tail latency SLOs
5) Cost regressions: tokens-per-call and model price-per-token changes impacting unit economics

SLOs and Alerting Thresholds (reference):
| Metric                      | Warning Threshold | Critical Threshold | Owner |
|---------------------------|-------------------:|-------------------:|-------|
| Median generation latency | 150 ms            | 300 ms            | SRE   |
| 95th generation latency   | 450 ms            | 900 ms            | SRE   |
| Functional pass rate      | -5% relative       | -10% relative     | ML Eng|
| Hallucination rate        | +2% absolute       | +5% absolute      | Applied ML |
| Average tokens/call       | +10% relative      | +25% relative     | Product |

Eval Harness Integration:
- All models must have a continuous eval job in the eval harness that runs the canonical prompt sets nightly and on every model build.
- Job naming convention: evals/{model_name}/{suite}/{daily|onbuild} e.g., evals/redwood-7b/qa/nightly
- Evals must emit metrics to the observability backend with the following tags: model_name, model_version, eval_suite, run_id, branch
- Failures in the eval harness produce GitHub PR checks (onbuild) and PagerDuty alerts (nightly critical threshold breaches)

Prompt Sets & Benchmarks (lifecycle):
1) Create: Prompt set owner writes intent doc, examples, and expected outputs (gold labels) in the prompt-sets repo.
2) Validate: Run local eval harness against the model (smoke test).
3) Approve: Peer review required (2 reviewers) and assign a reviewer from the product owner for task alignment.
4) Productionize: Upload to canonical prompt set registry and add to nightly eval suites.

Prompt set metadata (required fields):
- name (short-dash-format)
- task_description (one-sentence)
- owner (person/team)
- labels (list)
- expected_metric (e.g., accuracy, F1, BLEU)
- gold_data_location (s3:// or internal path)

Model Onboarding Checklist (minimum):
1) Model card: architecture, training data summary, known limitations, and recommended use-cases.
2) Quantization profile suggestion (see Quantization section).
3) Eval harness suites assigned: unit tests, integration open-domain, safety suite, latency benchmark.
4) Storage and artifact locations recorded (model store URI, sha256).
5) Canary rollout plan with success criteria and rollback steps.
6) Post-rollout monitoring dashboard and alert rules.

Quantization Profiles & Guidelines:
- Profiles are named by fidelity class: high-fidelity, balanced, cost-optim. Each profile includes recommended dtype (fp16/int8/llm.int8), activation quantization strategy, and fallback model variant.
- Rule of thumb: prefer balanced profile for customer-facing production (1-2% acceptable functional metric delta), cost-optim for internal-only or highly cost-sensitive batch use-cases.
- Run a quantization regression test: nightly quantized-vs-fp16 A/B eval across critical prompt sets.
- Quantization metadata required during onboarding: profile_name, quant_tool_version, QAT/NA, post-quantization metric delta (per-suite).

Regression Detection & Triage Playbook (high-level):
When an automated eval or SLO alert indicates a regression: 
1) Triage (first 15 minutes):
   a) Confirm signal: check eval harness logs and observability metrics for alert noise (false positives).
   b) Identify scope: which prompt sets, models, versions, and customers are affected.
2) Containment (15-60 minutes):
   a) If rollout-related, pause/rollback the rollout using deployment automation (canary -> previous stable).
   b) Apply temporary routing rules to shift traffic to a safe variant (e.g., older model or higher-fidelity profile).
3) Diagnosis (60-240 minutes):
   a) Re-run failing prompt sets locally and in a deterministic environment to reproduce the regression.
   b) Compare model artifacts (weights checksum, quant profiles) and infra changes (kernel/driver updates).
   c) Correlate with recent deploy/change events: model version, runtime kernel, CUDA/cudnn driver, scheduling change, autoscaler policy adjustments.
4) Remediation (same day where possible):
   a) If config/kernel/infra caused regression, roll forward fix or rotate drivers and run canary.
   b) If model-level degradation (quality), restore previous model version and open a model regression incident for the model owner.
5) Postmortem (within 3 working days):
   a) Standard incident review template must be completed and linked to the regression ticket.
   b) Identify preventive actions: new evals, tighter thresholds, or infra change approvals.

Regression Triage Runbook (step-by-step):
1) Open the regression incident ticket and assign owners (Model Owner, SRE lead, Observability owner).
2) Tag affected eval runs in the harness and export failing example set (max 200 examples) for human review.
3) Run parity comparisons (fp16 vs quantized) and baseline (previous production SHA) using the harness binary: 
   $ ./eval_harness run --suite failing-suite --model model_name --version current_sha --out /tmp/run.json
   $ ./eval_harness compare --baseline /tmp/baseline.json --current /tmp/run.json
4) Capture LLM internals where available: top-k logits, attention pattern diffs, estimated per-token probabilities for failing examples.
5) Decide mitigation: rollback, routing to safe_variant, or accept and monitor (rare).

Communication and Customer Impact:
- If >1% of customer-facing traffic is impacted or if there is a safety regression, notify Customer Success within 30 minutes and open a public-facing status note.
- Executive summary for severity-1 regressions required within 2 hours.

Rollout and Canary Guidance:
- Canary size: default 5% of traffic for major model upgrades; smaller for changes with mixed risk (1-2%).
- Canary duration: at least two 95th-latency+functional-eval cycles (typically 1-2 hours depending on traffic).
- Criteria to promote: no critical alerts, functional delta <= configured tolerance, and no increase in hallucination/safety flags.

Example Eval Configuration (YAML snippet, illustrative):
- suite: qa_regression_suite
  runs: nightly
  metrics: [accuracy, hallucination_rate, median_latency]
  thresholds:
    accuracy: {warning_delta: -3, critical_delta: -7}
    hallucination_rate: {warning_delta: +1, critical_delta: +3}

Appendix A — Example alert names and owners:
- evals.regression.critical -> PagerDuty: applied-ml-oncall
- model.latency.95p -> PagerDuty: infra-sre
- quant.regression.detected -> PagerDuty: applied-ml
